prompt: Company profile: Distribution company in Allentown, Pennsylvania; 200 employees at a single distribution center. Situation: The company hired a roofing contractor to replace the 30-foot-high flat roof. The contract runs six weeks. The company's own maintenance staff will periodically go onto the roof to escort the contractor and inspect progress, and they also access rooftop HVAC units for routine maintenance year-round. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
Here is the identification of compliance obligations for the company’s register, specifically tailored to the situation of a distribution center in Allentown, Pennsylvania, managing a roofing contractor and internal maintenance activities.

### 1. Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code (UCC) – Fall Protection Requirements

*   **Requirement:** Employees and contractors working on a low-slope roof (flat roof) with a height greater than 6 feet (this roof is 30 feet) must be protected from falling by one of the following systems: Guardrail systems, Safety net systems, or Personal fall arrest systems (PFAS). For work near the edge (within 6 feet), specific warning line systems or safety monitoring systems may be required.
*   **Source:** Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code (UCC) which adopts the **International Building Code (IBC)** and **OSHA Standards** (29 CFR 1926.501(b)(10) and 29 CFR 1910.28(b)(1)) as the enforceable safety standards in PA.
*   **Applicability:** This applies directly to the roofing contractor (contracted obligation) and the company's own maintenance staff who access the roof for inspections and HVAC maintenance. As the "host employer," the company has a duty to ensure the contractor is working safely and to protect its own employees.
*   **ISO Clause Map:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Legal requirements regarding worker safety).
*   **Evaluation (How & When):**
    *   *How:* Visual inspection of the roof perimeter to verify the presence of compliant fall protection (e.g., warning lines 6 feet from the edge, or guardrails) and verification that maintenance staff are utilizing proper tie-off points if guardrails are absent.
    *   *When:* Daily or weekly during the 6-week project duration; Ongoing annually for routine HVAC maintenance.

### 2. Pennsylvania Contractor Responsibility Act (Act 45)

*   **Requirement:** The company must verify that the roofing contractor holds a valid Pennsylvania Home Improvement Contractor registration number (if applicable to commercial work under local interpretation) and, more critically, maintains adequate general liability and workers' compensation insurance. The company must ensure the contractor is legally authorized to perform the work.
*   **Source:** **73 P.S. § 517.1 et seq.** (Pennsylvania Contractor Responsibility Act) and PA Workers' Compensation Act.
*   **Applicability:** The company is hiring an external contractor to perform work on its property. Failure to verify insurance and licensing can result in liability for the company if a worker is injured or property is damaged.
*   **ISO Clause Map:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Legal requirements regarding contractor management) and ISO 14001 6.1.3 (Legal requirements regarding liability).
*   **Evaluation (How & When):**
    *   *How:* Collection and filing of Certificates of Insurance (COI) naming the company as certificate holder; verification of PA registration status via the PA Attorney General’s database.
    *   *When:* Prior to the commencement of work (Pre-contract phase) and verification of renewal if the contract extends or for annual HVAC maintenance vendors.

### 3. OSHA Hazard Communication / Chemical Storage (Asbestos & Bitumen)

*   **Requirement:** If the existing roof contains hazardous materials (common in older flat roofs, e.g., asbestos-containing materials or old tar/bitumen), the company has an obligation to inform the contractor of the presence, location, and quantity of these materials. The company must ensure Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are available for materials on-site.
*   **Source:** **OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200)** and **EPA Asbestos NESHAP (40 CFR Part 61)**.
*   **Applicability:** The company is the building owner. Before the contractor disturbs the roof, the company must determine if hazardous building materials are present. This affects the internal maintenance staff who may encounter debris during their inspections.
*   **ISO Clause Map:** ISO 14001 6.1.3 (Environmental legal requirements regarding hazardous waste/substances) and ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Occupational health requirements).
*   **Evaluation (How & When):**
    *   *How:* Review of building records or conducting a hazardous building materials survey prior to construction; review of contractor’s disposal manifests.
    *   *When:* Prior to project start (Pre-contract) and during the project if unexpected materials are found.

### 4. Allentown/Pennsylvania Stormwater Management & Clean Water Act

*   **Requirement:** The company must prevent the discharge of pollutants (roofing debris, tar, adhesive containers) into the storm sewer system. Roofing projects often generate significant loose debris and chemical runoff. The company must ensure the contractor utilizes best management practices (BMPs) to keep debris out of storm drains.
*   **Source:** **Pennsylvania Clean Streams Law** and **City of Allentown Stormwater Management Ordinance** (Chapter 30 of Allentown Code). Also federal **Clean Water Act** if the facility operates under an MS4 permit.
*   **Applicability:** The distribution center likely has storm drains on the roof or in the parking lot surrounding the building. The company is responsible for preventing illicit discharges from their property.
*   **ISO Clause Map:** ISO 14001 6.1.3 (Environmental legal requirements).
*   **Evaluation (How & When):**
    *   *How:* Visual inspection of the site perimeter and storm drains to ensure no roofing debris or liquids are entering the drains; review of contractor’s site cleanup procedures.
    *   *When:* During and after significant rainfall events during the 6-week contract; daily site walks.

### 5. OSHA Walking-Working Surfaces (Internal Maintenance Staff)

*   **Requirement:** The company’s own maintenance staff accessing the HVAC units year-round must be provided with a safe means of access (fixed ladders or stairs) and fall protection. If the roof is accessed more than 4 times a year, a permanent fall protection system (e.g., guardrails or anchor points) is generally required.
*   **Source:** **OSHA General Industry Standard 29 CFR 1910, Subpart D (Walking-Working Surfaces)** and **29 CFR 1910.28**.
*   **Applicability:** The company has 200 employees and maintenance staff who access the roof "year-round." This creates a recurring hazard that requires engineering controls (guardrails) or administrative controls/Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
*   **ISO Clause Map:** ISO 45001 6.1.3 (Legal requirements regarding worker safety).
*   **Evaluation (How & When):**
    *   *How:* Annual audit of roof access points and fall protection systems; inspection of maintenance staff PPE (harnesses/lanyards).
    *   *When:* Annually (internal audit) and immediately following the roof replacement project to ensure new anchor points are certified.

### Summary of Compliance Evaluation Strategy (ISO 9.1.2)

To satisfy ISO 9.1.2, the company should establish a schedule that combines:
1.  **Pre-Project Verification:** Checking contractor insurance and permits before Day 1.
2.  **Active Monitoring:** Weekly site walks during the 6-week project to check for safety compliance (fall protection) and environmental compliance (stormwater).
3.  **Periodic Review:** An annual review of the roof access policy for internal staff to ensure it aligns with the new roof installation (e.g., are the new HVAC units accessible safely?).
